summary.title: Poseidon_Threat Model_new
summary.description: DFD for the project on Poseidon X

threats.title: Modbus AI Captain ID spoofing
threats.description: Mobus TCP lacks of authentication and integrity: an attacker can easily spoof the AI Captain IP if it reaches the OT network by requesting the ID's of who is connetcted though the modbus tcp. Then it can erease the register table and proceed to interact with the targeted victim (ECU) by identifying itself as the legitimate AI Captain
threats.mitigation: Micro-segmentation over OT network + allow-list of function code depending on sender ID

threats.title: Modbus AI Captain no audit trail of  request
threats.description: Mobus TCP lacks of authentication and integrity: an attacker can easily spoof the AI Captain IP if it reaches the OT network by requesting the ID's of who is connetcted though the modbus tcp. Then it can erease the register table and proceed to interact with the targeted victim (ECU) by identifying itself as the legitimate AI Captain
threats.mitigation: To ensure the audit trail of request, the system should implement an append-only DB for the logs of participants, which is computed by a cryptographically signed logging ( so that in case of an issue it is possible to retrieve the identity of the sender).

threats.title: Modbus AI Captain DoS
threats.description: AI Captian might not be able to provide request to the ECU via the Modbus TCP if it flooded by request from other sensors.
threats.mitigation: Apply a threshold rate of request from all sensors so that the AI Captain will not be blocked by flooding. Interaction from different sensors requires to be managed according to their priority.

threats.title: Modbus AI Captain Injection
threats.description: AI Captian might receive Modbus data packet tampered by an attacker as this protocol lacks of integrity check and authentication. An attacker, performing as a MITM, can change the ECU response (e.g. letting the AI CAptain receiving a false velocity) .
threats.mitigation: Migro-segmentation of the OT network + NIDS monitoring

threats.title: Modbus AI Captain Eavesdropping
threats.description: Data flow directed to AI Captain is not encrypted over Modbus TCP, thus an attacker can sniff or eavesdrop any information from ECU to AI Captain if it has access to OT network.
threats.mitigation: Migro-segmentation of the OT network + NIDS monitoring

threats.title: NavUnit Communication Spoofed
threats.description: Attacker can spoof the navunit identity letting the ai captain belive he is the authetic navigation unit.
threats.mitigation: authentication + logging to ensure mutual authentication ( implement handshake)

threats.title: AI logic currupted by tampered ECDIS
threats.description: AI model could received false data by a navigation unit whose ecdis system has been tampered
threats.mitigation: cross validating navigation info from other senors  and receivers for double checking

threats.title: NO audit of NavUnit info
threats.description: if the LAN and the DB  is not implemented to provide loggigin, it is not possible to recognize who is the author or the reader of a certain data. thus it is not possible to say who is responsible : if the ai captain made an error or if the navunit has given faulty data
threats.mitigation: provide NIDS+ LAN security with logging

threats.title: AI Captain vulnerability
threats.description: attacker can exploit parser vulnerability by injecting malicious code into the received data so when executed it will provide an elevetion of priviledge ( such as controll over linux system, buffer overlfow...)
threats.mitigation: ensure parser safety

threats.title: Navigation Info Eavesdropping
threats.description: if the attacker is able to listen to the communciation between navunit - ai captain an extrapolate important navigation info and decision
threats.mitigation: encrypting communication + LAN NIDS + authentication over lan

threats.title: Receiving false Position from GNSS
threats.description: Attacker that can access the physical connection between GNSS receiver and NAVUnit can impersonate the gnss receiver and send a fake position. this will lead the ECDIS to record and anlayze the area related to the fake position
threats.mitigation: physical access protection + NIDS + check coherency between last received positions

threats.title: NavUnit navigation info disclousure
threats.description: if NavUnit does not provide access control to the navigation DB, allowing the attacker to extract important information if it can access via physical or network level, or via the GNSS receiver and AIS receiver
threats.mitigation: enhanche security over NavUnit  network (NIDS + tamper evident cable + authentication between component)so unauthorized access will not be able to retrieve navigation documentation.

threats.title: GNSS position Lost
threats.description: If the GNSS is not working properly (because of physical attack, low signal or satellite jamming)  NavUnit will not receive a proper updated position which will result in a DoS as the navigation system would not work properly.
threats.mitigation: protection of GNSS receiver + use an IMU dead-rocking measurement to provide an inertial position until the connection with the satellite is restored

threats.title: NavUnit corruption because of gnss position
threats.description: If NavUnit receives a tampered or spoofed position from GNSS receiver l, this position  will currupt the ECDIS navigation system.
threats.mitigation: protection of GNSS receiver + use an IMU dead-rocking measurement to provide an inertial position until the connection to double check + alert if any incosistency arises

threats.title: ECDIS unauthorized access
threats.description: If an attacker can access the navigation network via LAN, the interface of the ECDIS and overpass its security,  it can obtain an elevation of privilege by being able to access the navigation unit as admin level. this it can overwrite the navigation chart, position and communication DB, disabling navigation alerts...
threats.mitigation: strong authentication for NavUnit management + firmware updated and verified + admin level accessible only from AI Captain or verified remote control.

threats.title: false AIS position
threats.description: VHF lacks of inegrity and authentication. Thus, an attacker can imitate another vessel to trick the PoseidonX into belivieng there is  or there is not an immidiate ship in a certain position.
threats.mitigation: implement also the usage of radar to double check

threats.title: ECDIS currupted by false AIS position
threats.description: if an attacker sends a fake position to AIS imitating the presence or the absence of a ship related to a certain position, the ECDIS navigation system will output decision based on uncorrect data.
threats.mitigation: double check with radar the surroundings + check for AIS tampering at physical and network level to avoid unauthorized access

threats.title: AIS communication Log lacking
threats.description: As VHF lacks of authenticity and logging, it is not possible to verify who is the author of a certain message. Thus, an attacker could imitate a certain ship, and that ship has no way to repudiate the attacker actions.
threats.mitigation: as the  AIS channel is meant to be public applying authentication process would distrupt the nature of this communication but it is possible to apply log using timestamps and WORM DB

threats.title: AIS communication lost
threats.description: AIS communication can be flooded by an attacker with false messages, so that the proper  communication between other vessels is interrupted. This could have catastrophical outcomes if our ship is not able to acknowledge the presence of an immidiate ship as the NavUnit wouldn't be able to use that info to calculate an emergency move
threats.mitigation: implement also the usage of radar to double check presence of immediate ships + maximum flow rate for ais receiver

threats.title: Satellite Communication Jamming
threats.description: Satellite communication works on L-Band frequency, which are very weak signaling. An attacker can overpower the legitimate signal by using stronger signal and impersonating the legitimate satellite. Thus, the received signal will not allow the receiver to alculate its position.
threats.mitigation: anti-jamming antenna + not relying on a single satellite but on a multi satellite constellation

threats.title: GNSS  satellite signal not authenticated
threats.description: Civillian Satellite signal is not verified by authentication nor digital signatur: thus, the receiver has no way to detect the legitimacy of the received signal.
threats.mitigation: enable cryptographic signing and logging over gnss

threats.title: GNSS  receiver tampering
threats.description: Internal/maintenance port of receiver might be subject to information disclosure attack as it might allow to retrieve internal information
threats.mitigation: physical access control to gnss receiver

threats.title: GNSS receiver Disconnection
threats.description: Physically disconnecting the receiver antenna will result in a D0s
threats.mitigation: Physical protection over intentional and unintentional reaceiver antenna

threats.title: GNSS receiver DoS
threats.description: DoS of GNSS receiver can be obtained by jamming the receiver antenna using overpowering signals
threats.mitigation: Anti-jamming antenna + multi satellite constallation

threats.title: Physically tampered GNSS receiver
threats.description: An attacker with physical access can modify the gnss receiver firmware so the ouput position will be inexact.
threats.mitigation: Physical access security check including periodic firmware check

threats.title: exploitation of firmware vulnerabilities
threats.description: Attacker can use malicious spoofed signal to exploit firmware vulnerabilities which might lead to a buffer overflow and thus the execution of malicious code
threats.mitigation: periodic firmware check and update + memory protection

threats.title: AIS communication Spoofing
threats.description: VHF lacks of inegrity and authentication. Thus, an attacker can imitate another vessel to trick the PoseidonX into belivieng there is  or there is not an immidiet ship in a certain position.
threats.mitigation: implement also the usage of radar to double check

threats.title: AIS communcation tampering
threats.description: if an attacker has physical access to the AIS receiver , it can modify its setting.
threats.mitigation: tamper evident cabling + nids+ unauthorized access protection from physical and LAN attacks

threats.title: AIS NO logs
threats.description: As VHF lacks of authenticity and logging, it is not possible to verify who is the author of a certain message. Thus, an attacker could imitate a certain ship, and that ship has no way to repudiate the attacker actions.
threats.mitigation: as the channel is meant to be public applying authentication process would distrupt the nature of this communication

threats.title: AIS Broadcast publicy
threats.description: AIS broadcastes our ship position constantly and this result in unknow receivers to acknowledge our psoition which might result in a privacy issue related to security of our ship.
threats.mitigation: no possible as this is the purpouse of the communication

threats.title: AIS Flooding
threats.description: if an attacker floods our ais receiver with a multitude of messages our systing will  be overwelmed and will not porcess the proper  information correclty ( ex other vessels)
threats.mitigation: set a limited rate for incoming messages + use of radar in case of flood

threats.title: PEP Proxy Spoofing
threats.description: Given that VSAT utilize performance proxies for TCP acceleration, an adversary could masquerade as the shore-based PEP server to intercept vessel handshakes.
threats.mitigation: Implement End-to-End Network-Layer Encryption (IPsec VPN), Strict PEP Bypass Configurations, and Cryptographic TCP-AO (TCP Authentication Option).

threats.title: Firmware Tampering
threats.description: Deploying malicious firmware to the vessel's VSAT modem to establish a persistent backdoor via external actors.
threats.mitigation: Implement Cryptographic Firmware Code Signing (Secure Boot), Strict Management Interface Isolation, and Remote Attestation and Integrity Monitoring.

threats.title: Exposed Interface Leakage
threats.description: VSAT terminals exposing HTTP diagnostic interfaces to the public internet can reveal firmware versions and vessel coordinates.
threats.mitigation: Implement Public Interface Disabling and WAN-side Firewalls, Cryptographic Management Access (HTTPS/SSH), and Shodan/Censys Surface Monitoring.

threats.title: Volumetric DDos
threats.description: Saturating the limited bandwidth of the maritime VSAT link by flooding the modem's public IP with junk packets like SYN floods.
threats.mitigation: Implement Upstream DDoS Scrubbing and SYN Cookies, Strict Firewall TCP Intercept/Rate Limiting, and Carrier-Grade Private APN Network Architecture.

threats.title: VSAT Terminal Pivoting
threats.description: Exploiting the satellite router to gain guest access and escalating to admin privileges. This allows lateral movement from IT communication systems to OT networks controlling propulsion.
threats.mitigation: Implement Strict Air-Gapped Network Segmentation (Conduits and Zones), Robust Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) & Hardened Firmwares, and Operational Technology Network Intrusion Detection Systems (OT-IDS).

threats.title: Traffic hijacking
threats.description: An attacker gaining access to the SatLink administrative interface could potentially modify the tunnel configuration to route traffic to a malicious external server
threats.mitigation: Implement Cryptographic Configuration Integrity Verification, Centralized Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), and Immutable Out-of-Band Config Backups.

threats.title: Service impersonation
threats.description: Malicious external servers impersonate legitimate services (like Netflix or Email) to steal crew credentials over the unencrypted internet flow.
threats.mitigation: Implement Enforced HTTPS Everywhere / HSTS, Secure DNS with Phishing Protection, and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for Ship Systems.

threats.title: AI Captain Impersonation through Modbus
threats.description: Modbus TCP is protocol that lacks of authentication and encryption, thus if an attacker can apply spoofing to imitate a legitimate network component by sniffing its ID, to send un-authenticated data.
threats.mitigation: Micro-segmentation over OT network + allow-list of function code depending on sender ID

threats.title: AI Request Tampering
threats.description: As there is no authentication or check of integrity over a received request, an attacker can inject a legitimate AI Captain request and overide the function code to obtain a desired behaviour .

threats.title: ECU no audit trail of received request
threats.description: As authentication is not implemented in Modbus TCP the AI Captain suffers from insufficient logging: thus, it is not possible to check if a problematic request has been issued by a legitimate component or a malicious one.
threats.mitigation: To ensure the audit trail of request, the system should implement a DB for the requests and a logging process for the participants ( so that in case of an issue it is possible to retrieve the identity of the sender).

threats.title: PCL  ECU register overwriting
threats.description: As there is no authentication or check of integrity over a received request, an attacker can scan the OT network and find the PCL port. Thus, it can tamper a request from the AI Captain to override the PCL firmware by changing ECU register values.
threats.mitigation: Engineering port physically disabled at least during travelling + requires two-person authorization to physically access it.

threats.title: Accessing through Engineering port to  overide security logic of PLC
threats.description: As there is no authentication or check of integrity over a received request, an attacker can scan the OT network and find the PCL port and its hardware finger print.  Then it can use the vendor software to override completely the PLC logic.
threats.mitigation: Engineering port physically disabled at least during travelling + requires two-person authorization to physically access it.

threats.title: ECU overflooding
threats.description: As there is no authentication or check of integrity over a received request, an attacker can scan the OT network and find the PCL port and its hardware finger print.
threats.mitigation: Engineering port physically disabled at least during travelling + requires two-person authorization to physically access it.

threats.title: ECU Register Eavesdrop
threats.description: As there is no authentication or check of integrity over a received request, an attacker can access the ECU register values by sending/tampering a request to the ECU and using the Function Code related to the read holding register (e.g. current velocity, rpm...).
threats.mitigation: Apply an allowed-function code list over a OT Firewall in combination with a OT micro-segmentation: This will ensure that certain request (e.g write) will be allowed iff sent by the legitimate AI Captain, and that the data flows only through AI Captain and ECU and no futher entity.

threats.title: AI captain impersonification
threats.description: By spoofing the MAC or IP identity of the Linux-based AI Captain process.
threats.mitigation: By deploying an Intrusion Prevention System on the switch to detect unauthorized MAC or IP address reuse.

threats.title: Physical tampering
threats.description: By making unauthorized adjustments to the vessel's water distribution and stabilization mechanism
threats.mitigation: By enforcing a two person rule physical access policies for the engine room to mitigate insider threat risks.

threats.title: Firmware tampering
threats.description: Zigbee gateway lacks secure boot and firmware validation; an attacker with physical or network access can flash malicious firmware.
threats.mitigation: Implement secure boot , require signed firmware updates, and restrict physical access to the gateway enclosure.

threats.title: Physical tampering
threats.description: An attacker with physical access can attach debugging interfaces, extract cryptographic keys, or physically break the device
threats.mitigation: Enforce tamper‑evident seals, place gateway in a locked cabinet, and monitor physical access logs.

threats.title: Rogue AP
threats.description: An attacker within range sets up a fake Wi‑Fi network with the same SSID, tricking crew members into connecting and revealing credentials or injecting malware.
threats.mitigation: Use WPA3‑Enterprise with certificate validation, implement Rogue AP detection on the main router.

threats.title: Packet injection
threats.description: By injecting unauthorized wireless data packets directly into the broadcast spectrum.
threats.mitigation: By enabling strict wireless client isolation to completely prevent connected devices from interacting or injecting packets into one another.

threats.title: Eavesdropping
threats.description: By monitoring the private web browsing traffic, personal communications, and unencrypted session tokens of the crew
threats.mitigation: By mandating the use of secure application layer encryption protocols like HTTPS, SSH, or VPNs for all connected devices.

threats.title: Signal jamming
threats.description: By deploying a physical radio jamming device near the vessel's living quarters to flood the 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz wireless channels.
threats.mitigation: By utilizing dual band or tri band access points that dynamically shift traffic across 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz spectrums.

threats.title: De-auth attack
threats.description: By spoofing the MAC address of the wireless access point to transmit de-authentication frames over the air.
threats.mitigation: By deploying a Wireless Intrusion Prevention System to actively detect and flag abnormal spikes in de-authentication frames.

threats.title: Vessels Position eavesdropping
threats.description: as VHF radio does not provide encryption and it is meant to allow to  publicy disclose immediate ship position, an attacker can exploit this communication to eavesdrop.
threats.mitigation: no mitigation as is meant to be public for security reason

threats.title: VHF Jammig
threats.description: as VHF radio is public and lacks of authentication, it can suffer from frquency jamming: an attacker can continuously occupy the frequency related to a specific channel to avoid other ships to engage with the communication
threats.mitigation: anti-jamming antenna

threats.title: Telemetry Leakage
threats.description: Telemetry Leakage refers to the unauthorized interception or exposure of sensitive maritime data as it travels between the vessel and the RCC.
threats.mitigation: Implement Standard VPN Encapsulation, Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS), End-to-End Application Encryption, and Traffic Padding.

threats.title: Unauthorized Directives
threats.description:
This threat involves an adversary transmitting illegitimate navigation or operational instructions to the vessel's onboard systems. An actor may falsify IP addresses or compromise the Remote Operations Center (RCC) to send these unauthorized directives to the onboard router.
(Tampering/spoofing)
threats.mitigation: Implement Mutual TLS (mTLS), Application-Layer Command Signing (HSM), and Strict Firewall Whitelisting.

threats.title: Signal jamming/bandwidth flooding
threats.description: The VSAT link could disconnect the ship from the RCC, forcing the crew to take manual control.
threats.mitigation: Implement Multi-Provider Satellite Redundancy (Dual-Band VSAT/LEO), Automated Safe-State Failover Modes, and RF Jamming Detection and Direction Finding.

threats.title: TCP packet tampering
threats.description: Absent robust end-to-end encryption over the VSAT link, attackers may alter packets in transit, potentially modifying waypoints or falsifying LiDAR sensor telemetry.
threats.mitigation: Implement Cryptographic Message Authentication (HMAC), End-to-End Tunnel Encryption (IPsec/TLS), and Sensor Data Plausibility Checks.

threats.title: Data tampering
threats.description: An attacker with access to the ship’s internal network can perform a man-in-the-middle attack to intercept and modify temperature records before they are stored.
threats.mitigation: Network micro-segmentation and TLS encryption for data in transit.

threats.title: Replay Attack
threats.description: An attacker could capture legitimate temperature packets and replay them later to mask a real‑time incident
threats.mitigation: Include a timestamp and sequence number in each record, and reject out‑of‑order messages

threats.title: Bandwidth Exhaustion
threats.description: High-bandwidth usage on the Crew Wi-Fi (e.g., Netflix streaming) could saturate the physical SatLink connection.
threats.mitigation: Implement Strict Bandwidth Hard-Cap Limits, Application-Layer Traffic Shaping, and Strict Quality of Service (QoS) Prioritization.

threats.title: VLAN Hooping
threats.description: Due to the shared physical antenna and router, a VLAN Hopping attack could allow crew members to sniff ship telemetry data from the Crew Wi-Fi network.
threats.mitigation: Implement Strict Trunk Port Disabling & Native VLAN Modification, Enforced Hardware-Level Network Isolation, and Dynamic MAC-to-VLAN Mapping.

threats.title: VLAN hopping
threats.description: An attacker on the crew Wi‑Fi VLAN exploits a misconfiguration to jump to the telemetry VLAN.
threats.mitigation: Enforce VLAN access control lists and use explicit “deny” rules between VLANs.

threats.title: DNS redirection
threats.description: An attacker on the crew VLAN could send fake DNS responses to redirect crew traffic to malicious sites or intercept telemetry.
threats.mitigation: Implement DNSSEC validation on the router and enable DHCP snooping to prevent rogue DNS servers.

threats.title: Man in the middle
threats.description: By physically placing an unauthorized device between the AI Captain and the controllers.
threats.mitigation: By implementing static ARP tables on both the AI Captain and the controllers to prevent ARP poisoning attacks.

threats.title: Packet flooding
threats.description: By consuming all available network bandwidth between the AI Captain and the controllers.
threats.mitigation: By implementing rate limiting policies to drop network traffic that exceeds a specified packet per second threshold.

threats.title: Packet sniffing
threats.description: By attaching an unauthorized device to a physical port on the internal Ethernet switch.
threats.mitigation: By disabling unused physical ports on the internal Ethernet switch to prevent unauthorized hardware attachments.

threats.title: Signal jamming
threats.description: By deploying a physical radio jamming device near the vessel to flood the 2.4 GHz wireless channel.
threats.mitigation: By implementing channel hopping, allowing the system to switch to a cleaner radio channel if a high signal-to-noise ratio is detected.

threats.title: Eavesdropping
threats.description: By deploying a wireless packet sniffer within radio range of the vessel to capture traffic.
threats.mitigation: By utilizing unique cryptographic codes on each reefer sensor for pairing.

threats.title: Battery exhaustion
threats.description: By forcing the low power container sensors to continuously stay in an active, high-drain state.
threats.mitigation: By implementing rate limiting on the Zigbee Gateway to ignore repeating broadcast requests.

threats.title: Tampering
threats.description: By altering the temperature or humidity data payload before it reaches the ship's network.
threats.mitigation: By using frame counters in the network layer to detect and reject altered or out of order packets.

threats.title: Network flooding
threats.description: By overwhelming the central Zigbee Gateway with continuous packets.
threats.mitigation: By implementing rate limiting features on the Zigbee Gateway to drop traffic exceeding a packet threshold.

threats.title: Modbus Injection
threats.description: Modbus TCP does not have any authentication protocol. Thus, it is possible for an attacker to inject maliciously the data flow between AI Captain and ECU, with the scope to alter the Engine Controller values and security threshold. This attack exploits the usage of the function code in Modbus Data Packet.
threats.mitigation: Apply an allowed-function code list over a OT Firewall in combination with a OT micro-segmentation: This will ensure that certain request (e.g write) will be allowed iff sent by the legitimate AI Captain, and that the data flows only through AI Captain and ECU and no futher entity.

threats.title: ModBus EavesDropping
threats.description: Modbus TCP is protocol that lacks of authentication and encryption, thus if an attacker can eavesdrop or sniff the data flow between components, it will understand every Modbus Data Packed content.
threats.mitigation: Network Micro-segmentation of OT will ensure that only authorized component can access the data flow over Modbus TCP ( e.g AI Captain and ECU)

threats.title: Modbus TCP Flooding
threats.description: Modbus TCP protocol, does not implement any threshold for the request rate over its channel. As this protocol works as a client-server protocol, a flooding request rate will result as a DoS
threats.mitigation: Implementing a safe threshold rate over the OT network firewall will ensure to avoid this attack.

threats.title: Satellite Signal Disclousure
threats.description: Satellite signal has no encryption, so anyone receiving it has access to its information.
threats.mitigation: not necessary as the communication is ment to be public

threats.title: Satellite Communication Jamming
threats.description: Satellite communication works on L-Band frequency, which are very weak signaling. An attacker can overpower the legitimate signal by using stronger signal and impersonating the legitimate satellite. Thus, the received signal will not allow the receiver to alculate its position.
threats.mitigation: anti-jamming antenna + not relying on a single satellite but on a multi satellite constellation

threats.title: RF Eavesdropping
threats.description: Given the vast satellite footprint, unencrypted TCP/IP traffic can be sniffed, exposing passwords, maritime telemetry, and cargo load plans.
threats.mitigation: Provide remediation for this threat or a reason if status is N/A

threats.title: Vessel Position Tampering
threats.description: If an attacker has physical access to the connection or can modify it by accessing to the LAN, it can modify the data, letting the navigation system work with erroneus data.
threats.mitigation: protecting the LAN access by ensuring protection from unauthorized entity + NIDS + ensuring the communciation is authenticated and only between NavUnit and AIS

threats.title: Vessel Position  disclousure
threats.description: an attacker with physical acces to the connection or via LAN access, can listen the data about ships's positions.
threats.mitigation: provide encryption and authentication  + NIDS to avoid unauthorized accesses + tamper evident connection

threats.title: Vessel Position DoS
threats.description: If an attacker has physical access to the connection or can modify it by accessing to the LAN, it can physically unable the connection by ruining the cables . This can also happen because of interface mulfunctioning.
threats.mitigation: protecting the LAN access by ensuring protection from unauthorized entity + NIDS + periodict cable and interface maintenance

threats.title: External Dos
threats.description: A Distributed Denial of Service attack from the internet targeting the ship's public IP, saturating the VSAT bandwidth
threats.mitigation: Implement Upstream DDoS Scrubbing Services, Traffic Rate Limiting & Strict QoS, and Private APN / Non-Public IP Addressing.

threats.title: Malicius code injection
threats.description:
Injecting malware into unencrypted HTTP traffic requested by the crew, potentially compromising devices that share the ship's physical infrastructure.
A compromised crew device serves as an ideal staging ground for attackers to launch lateral internal attacks.
threats.mitigation: Implement Strict DNS Filtering & Secure Web Gateways, Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) Deep Packet Inspection, and Isolated Out-of-Band VLAN Termination.

threats.title: VLAN Hopping
threats.description: Because the main router separates crew Wi‑Fi and telemetry via VLAN, an attacker on the crew network could exploit double‑tagging to access the ZigBee subnet.
threats.mitigation: Disable native VLAN on trunk ports and use private VLANs.

threats.title: Man in the middle
threats.description: An attacker on the same subnet as the gateway could poison ARP tables and redirect traffic to their own machine, then tamper with or drop container data.
threats.mitigation: Enable Dynamic ARP Inspection on the router, static ARP entries for critical devices, and enforce HTTPS/TLS for all traffic.

threats.title: Malicious code Injection
threats.description: attacker could inject malicious code that once read by navUnit would infect the system
threats.mitigation: intruision detection on LAN + NIDS

threats.title: eavesdropping navigation charts
threats.description: if the LAN and the DB  is not implemented to provide loggigin, it is not possible to recognize who is the author or the reader of a certain data
threats.mitigation: provide NIDS+ LAN security with logging

threats.title: Connection with db flood
threats.description: attacker floods the db with multiple request or query, so that our system is not able to access the navigation charts.
threats.mitigation: request rate limitation on DB write access + WORM memory (or read only)

threats.title: Communication with DB tampered
threats.description: attacker with access (remote or physical) to the LAN is able to intercept the communication between DB of navigation charts and AI captain: thus, the attacker can inject the communication with false and malicious data
threats.mitigation: NIDS + atuthentication and logging between two components + only read during travel + update of the charts only at authorized base

threats.title: info eavesdropping
threats.description: attacker with access to LAN that does not ensure logging or encryption can listen though this channel.
threats.mitigation: as this are not striclty confidential data, we might just implement encryption

threats.title: request and query flood
threats.description: attacker with access to LAN can flood the navigation db with request and query. thus the ai captain request for navigation chart data will not be responded
threats.mitigation: request/query rate limted + only read + backup db

threats.title: RCC Spoofing
threats.description: An actor may falsify IP addresses or compromise Remote Operations Center to transmit unauthorized navigation directives to the onboard router
threats.mitigation: Implement Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication, IP White-listing (Geo-fencing), and Hardware-based Command Signing.

threats.title: Command log deletion
threats.description: Lack of robust logging at the RCC could allow a remote operator to deny sending a command that caused a "catastrophic failure". (from the proposal file)
threats.mitigation: Implement Centralized, Cryptographically Signed WORM (Write-Once-Read-Many) Logging with strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).

threats.title: Crew member impersonification
threats.description: By an unauthorized actor stealing legitimate crew credentials, session tokens, or personal devices.
threats.mitigation: By enforcing strict multi factor authentication for all crew accounts and system access portals.

threats.title: Repudiation
threats.description: By performing unauthorized configuration modifications or sending malicious requests from a crew device.
threats.mitigation: By forwarding all crew network connection logs and authentication to an external system via SatLink.

threats.title: Gnss Position tampering
threats.description: If an attacker has physical access to the connection or can modify it by accessing to the LAN, it can modify the data, letting the navigation system work with erroneus data.
threats.mitigation: protecting the LAN access by ensuring protection from unauthorized entity + NIDS + ensuring the communciation is authenticated and only between NavUnit and GNSS

threats.title: Gnss Position disclosure
threats.description: an attacker with physical acces to the connection or via LAN access, can listen the data about ships's positions.
threats.mitigation: provide encryption and authentication  + NIDS to avoid unauthorized accesses + tamper evident connection

threats.title: Gnss DoS
threats.description: If an attacker has physical access to the connection or can modify it by accessing to the LAN, it can physically unable the connection by ruining the cables . This can also happen because of interface mulfunctioning.
threats.mitigation: protecting the LAN access by ensuring protection from unauthorized entity + NIDS + periodict cable and interface maintenance

threats.title: SQL Injection
threats.description: An attacker could exploit a vulnerability to execute SQL commands, reading or deleting records.
threats.mitigation: Use parametrised queries and sanitise all inputs

threats.title: Query flooding
threats.description: An attacker could issue a large number of complex queries to exhaust database CPU and memory, preventing legitimate writes from the ZigBee gateway.
threats.mitigation: Implement query rate limiting and connection pooling with max concurrent queries.

threats.title: Elevation of privilege
threats.description: Exploiting a vulnerability in the Main Router’s firmware from the Crew Wi-Fi VLAN to gain administrative access to the Engineering/OT subnet.
threats.mitigation: Implement Continuous Firmware Patch Management & Vulnerability Scanning, Hardware-Isolated Router Architecture (Physical Air-Gapping), and Local Out-of-Band Administrative Management.

threats.title: ARP spoofing
threats.description: An attacker sends falsified ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) messages to link their MAC address with the IP address of the AI Captain or SatLink. This redirects traffic through the attacker's device, enabling a Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack.
threats.mitigation: Implement Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI), Static ARP Binding for Critical Assets, and Strict Layer-2 Port Isolation (Private VLANs).
